title: DRC Ebola Toll Reported at 5,514 Cases, 2,690+ Deaths as CFR Climbs to 47.9%
detail: Africanews reported on 25 August 2026 that DRC's Ebola case count had reached 5,514 confirmed cases with more than 2,690 deaths, a case-fatality rate of 47.9% — up from roughly 47.6% a week earlier — citing WHO's continued 'very high' risk rating for DRC (the only country at that level) alongside 'high' risk designations for nine bordering states including Burundi and the Central African Republic. The update came a day after WHO confirmed its IHR Emergency Committee had voted on 24 August to maintain the outbreak's PHEIC status and issue updated cross-border recommendations. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus had said on 18 August that the outbreak 'was spreading more quickly than any previous one.'

media.caption: DRC's Ebola death toll climbs past 2,690 as WHO maintains 'very high' risk rating and expands cross-border guidance

title: WHO Officially Declares Uganda's 2026 Ebola Outbreak Over After 42-Day Countdown
detail: During a joint press briefing with Uganda's Ministry of Health on 25 August 2026, WHO officially declared the end of Uganda's 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, confirming completion of the mandatory 42-day monitoring period (twice the virus's maximum incubation period) without a new confirmed case since the last patient was discharged from care on 16 July 2026. This international declaration follows Uganda's own earlier administrative announcement on 28 July 2026, made ahead of the standard 42-day window based on completed epidemiological investigation and contact tracing. Uganda's outbreak totaled 20 confirmed cases (15 imported from DRC, 5 locally acquired), 18 recoveries and 2 deaths. WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said 'Uganda has demonstrated that with decisive action, Ebola outbreaks can be brought under control quickly.' The DRC outbreak that seeded Uganda's cases continues to escalate with no end in sight.

media.caption: WHO confirms Uganda's 2026 Ebola outbreak is over after completing the 42-day monitoring period
